items.q: What are the formal elements of art?
items.correct: Line, shape, form, tone, texture, pattern, colour and space.
items.random_wrong: Just whether a drawing looks neat.
items.why: The formal elements are the building blocks artists use and combine.

items.q: Can the primary colours be mixed from other colours?
items.correct: No — red, yellow and blue can't be mixed from others; they make secondary colours.
items.misconception: Yes, you can mix primary colours from other colours.
items.why: Primaries are the starting points; mixing them produces secondary colours like green and orange.

items.correct: The range from light to dark, used to create form and depth.
items.misconception: Filling everything with one flat colour.
items.why: Varying tone (shading) makes objects look three-dimensional.

items.q: Does good artwork need planning and development?
items.correct: Yes — artists develop ideas through studies, experiments and refinement.
items.misconception: No, the first attempt is always the final piece.
items.random_wrong: Only the final image matters, never the process.
items.why: The creative process (research, studies, refinement) is central to art courses.
